paper.title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions
paper.central_claim: POET pairs a population of evolving environments with ES-optimised agents and transfers agents between environments, generating and solving increasingly challenging, diverse 2-D obstacle courses that direct ES optimisation or a single-path curriculum cannot reach; transfer is essential.
paper.scope_reason: Closed loop on a non-weight object (environment population) plus weight training of solvers; not 'improver update and product both weights' (A3 bullet 1). Inclusion rests on the frozen boundary card; see revision proposal.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Within a capped 2-D terrain encoding, POET's feedback-filtered, retained environment population with cross-niche transfer reaches solved environments that ES-from-scratch and an ancestor-budget single-path curriculum do not reach at the hardest levels, and transfer-off runs solve no extremely challenging environments (3 vs 3 runs).

G.reason: Specific residual against MCC (no within-niche optimisation, only currently-solvable problems kept) and Innovation Engine/CMOEA/QD (static environments), plus single-path curricula; the fixed non-weight object (hand-posed environment) is named. Neighbours are only characterised from this paper's own text.

M.reason: Mechanism chain (eligibility -> mutate -> MC band 50-300 -> novelty rank -> ES -> transfer) is reconstructable and yields distinguishable predictions vs ES-only, direct-path and no-transfer. Revised from sol's 4 for calibration consistency with Voyager/STOP: the load-bearing operating assumptions (MC band as 'learnable', genotype-space novelty as useful diversity, ES-step count as the resource unit) are hand-set heuristics without justification or sensitivity analysis.

X.reason: MUTATE_ENVS / EVALUATE_CANDIDATES, capacity queue with oldest-first removal, seeds, archive and transfer-replacement rule are specified; full hyperparameter schedule and any external certification of the curriculum are not.

E.measurement.reason: Simulator return with an explicit solved criterion (reach end and score>=230) is a trustworthy verifier; difficulty levels and coverage are measured in genotype space, which is a proxy for behavioural diversity, so not 4.

E.causality.reason: ES-from-scratch, direct-path curriculum and transfer-off controls exist; the direct-path budget counts only ancestor-line ES steps (not other branches or transfer evaluations), so the multi-path advantage is confounded with total compute (A2: budget defect here and in E.cost only).

E.holdout.reason: Targets are sampled from environments POET itself generated and solved, so selection and test coincide; no frozen curriculum is certified on an independent task family.

E.statistics.reason: Three full POET runs (plus three transfer-off), five control runs per target, 95% CIs, Mann-Whitney U and one-sample t-tests: ladder level 3 (A2), though the one-score-vs-distribution t-test is weak.

E.cost.reason: 256 cores x ~10 days per run and ES-step budgets reported; controls are not charged the full parallel search/transfer cost.

resolutions.reason: Once in scope, the author claim (open-ended, unbounded) exceeds the evidence; the scoped claim above is supported. son55's 'unresolved' was a consequence of its scope exclusion.
Main-card signature fits (fixed environment liberated); son55 left it empty only because it excluded the paper.
No C-sub tactic applies (C15/C23/C24 are generative-model internals).
H23 tactic explicitly covers procedural generators with difficulty windows and stepping-stone archives; H22 (trained proposer) does not apply. Fit lowered to medium.

Controls present, no outside-loop task family.

sol's 4 lowered: key operating assumptions are untested heuristics (see rating reason); applied the same standard used for Voyager/STOP M.
Verified simulator success criterion; genotype-space coverage is a proxy.
Verified ancestor-line-only budget for the direct-path control.
Verified post-hoc target selection from POET's own solved set.

A3 'evaluated object' test: the loop changes and retains a non-weight object (environment population/archive) using execution feedback, and that object is evaluated directly (direct-path curriculum control, coverage of environments created and solved). It is therefore not 'improver update and product both weights' (A3 bullet 1). Weight training of solvers does not exclude it (A3 bullet 2). son55's 'only serves weight training' argument would exclude the whole frozen boundary card self_generate_the_curriculum; per A3 bullet 3 such exclusion must go through an explicit card revision, which is filed as a revision proposal.
POET is itself a closed loop (feedback -> candidate environments -> MC accept/reject -> retained population -> next iteration), not a pluggable component; class A, flagged as L1 boundary.

aggregate_review.initial_judgment_before_seat_scores: Two co-evolving populations: ES-trained controller weights and terrain encodings mutated by a fixed operator, admitted by a success band on current agents, novelty-ranked and retained (active queue + archive). The environment set is both training curriculum and an evaluated product (direct-path control, coverage). Evidence is task-level: targets come from POET's own solved set.
